text:
The stock was essentially flat today, closing just 0.07% higher at $474, but the two-week rally of 9.6% reflects a sharp rebound from lows around $433 in early October. The underlying driver has been oil prices: Brent crude topped $109 per barrel on October 19th after Houthi militants claimed attacks on Saudi Arabian airports and Aramco facilities, and the U.S. oil price now sits at $101.91 per barrel. For a refiner like this, higher crude prices initially pressure margins, but the recent rally suggests markets are pricing in tighter global supply from Middle East disruption risk—and refineries running at 93.5% utilization are positioned to capture value if crude stays elevated while demand holds.

The escalating geopolitical tension in the Strait of Hormuz and repeated Houthi attacks have created uncertainty, which can cut both ways. Today's modest decline came as traders reportedly grew hopeful about diplomatic progress, which would ease supply concerns and potentially lower oil prices—the opposite of what has driven the recent rally. The stock remains well above early October lows, so the 9.6% gain likely reflects net positioning for a period of tighter global crude supply rather than conviction about where prices settle long-term.
